answer: Force every pair of identities to bargain before they can share a reward: split terms, counteroffers, deadlines, walk-aways. A lone operator running a farm negotiates with itself, so its deals close instantly and identically, like a willow that never bends because no wind touches it. Real pairs haggle unevenly — pauses, partial concessions, a deal balanced on a narrow ledge — and the pulse of that friction is hard to fake at scale: scripting a hundred distinct, plausible negotiations costs the operator more attention than the sybils earn.
